//! A bounded kernel heap with a static bootstrap arena and optional frame-backed growth.
//!
//! The bootstrap arena is 256 KiB and tracks at most 128 allocations. An optional
//! extension maps pages on demand inside a caller-reserved virtual range, with
//! its own fixed allocation table and a caller-supplied transactional mapper.
//! Growth is bounded; allocation fails when either arena or metadata is full.
//!
//! The global wrapper serializes access with an IRQ-save spin lock. The lock
//! prevents a local interrupt from re-entering a held allocator lock; allocation
//! remains forbidden in IRQ/exception context to keep handlers bounded and
//! allocation-free.

use crate::sync::{IrqSpinLock, IrqSpinLockGuard};
use core::alloc::{GlobalAlloc, Layout};
use core::cell::UnsafeCell;
use core::ptr::NonNull;

/// Fixed capacity of the initial BSS-backed kernel heap.
pub const KERNEL_HEAP_CAPACITY: usize = 256 * 1024;
/// Maximum number of live allocations tracked by the initial kernel heap.
pub const KERNEL_HEAP_MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize = 128;

/// The statically allocated heap type used by the kernel binary.
pub type KernelHeap = LockedHeap<KERNEL_HEAP_CAPACITY, KERNEL_HEAP_MAX_ALLOCATIONS>;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum HeapError {
    ZeroSizedAllocation,
    AllocationTableFull,
    OutOfMemory,
    AddressOverflow,
    InvalidPointer,
    LayoutMismatch,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct Allocation {
    start: usize,
    size: usize,
    alignment: usize,
}

struct FixedHeap<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> {
    arena: [u8; HEAP_SIZE],
    allocations: [Option<Allocation>; MAX_ALLOCATIONS],
}

impl<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> FixedHeap<HEAP_SIZE, MAX_ALLOCATIONS> {
    const fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            arena: [0; HEAP_SIZE],
            allocations: [None; MAX_ALLOCATIONS],
        }
    }

    fn allocate(&mut self, layout: Layout) -> Result<NonNull<u8>, HeapError> {
        if layout.size() == 0 {
            return Err(HeapError::ZeroSizedAllocation);
        }
        let slot = self
            .allocations
            .iter()
            .position(Option::is_none)
            .ok_or(HeapError::AllocationTableFull)?;
        let start = self.find_gap(layout)?;
        self.allocations[slot] = Some(Allocation {
            start,
            size: layout.size(),
            alignment: layout.align(),
        });

        let pointer = self.arena.as_mut_ptr().wrapping_add(start);
        NonNull::new(pointer).ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)
    }

    fn deallocate(&mut self, pointer: NonNull<u8>, layout: Layout) -> Result<(), HeapError> {
        if layout.size() == 0 {
            return Err(HeapError::ZeroSizedAllocation);
        }
        let arena_start = self.arena.as_ptr() as usize;
        let allocation_start = (pointer.as_ptr() as usize)
            .checked_sub(arena_start)
            .filter(|offset| *offset < HEAP_SIZE)
            .ok_or(HeapError::InvalidPointer)?;

        for allocation in &mut self.allocations {
            let Some(active) = *allocation else {
                continue;
            };
            if active.start != allocation_start {
                continue;
            }
            if active.size != layout.size() || active.alignment != layout.align() {
                return Err(HeapError::LayoutMismatch);
            }
            *allocation = None;
            return Ok(());
        }
        Err(HeapError::InvalidPointer)
    }

    fn find_gap(&self, layout: Layout) -> Result<usize, HeapError> {
        let arena_start = self.arena.as_ptr() as usize;
        let mut candidate = 0usize;

        loop {
            let candidate_address = arena_start
                .checked_add(candidate)
                .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
            let aligned_address = candidate_address
                .checked_add(layout.align() - 1)
                .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?
                & !(layout.align() - 1);
            let start = aligned_address
                .checked_sub(arena_start)
                .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
            let end = start
                .checked_add(layout.size())
                .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
            if end > HEAP_SIZE {
                return Err(HeapError::OutOfMemory);
            }

            let mut conflicting_end = None;
            for allocation in self.allocations.iter().flatten() {
                let allocation_end = allocation
                    .start
                    .checked_add(allocation.size)
                    .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
                if start < allocation_end && allocation.start < end {
                    conflicting_end = Some(
                        conflicting_end
                            .map_or(allocation_end, |end: usize| end.max(allocation_end)),
                    );
                }
            }

            match conflicting_end {
                Some(end) => candidate = end,
                None => return Ok(start),
            }
        }
    }
}

pub type HeapPageMapper = unsafe fn(context: *mut (), first_page: usize, page_count: usize) -> bool;

struct FrameBackedHeap<const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> {
    base: usize,
    capacity_pages: usize,
    mapped_pages: usize,
    allocations: [Option<Allocation>; MAX_ALLOCATIONS],
    context: *mut (),
    map_pages: Option<HeapPageMapper>,
}

impl<const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> FrameBackedHeap<MAX_ALLOCATIONS> {
    const fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            base: 0,
            capacity_pages: 0,
            mapped_pages: 0,
            allocations: [None; MAX_ALLOCATIONS],
            context: core::ptr::null_mut(),
            map_pages: None,
        }
    }

    fn configure(
        &mut self,
        base: usize,
        capacity_pages: usize,
        context: *mut (),
        map_pages: HeapPageMapper,
    ) -> Result<(), FrameHeapInitError> {
        let capacity = capacity_pages
            .checked_mul(PAGE_BYTES)
            .and_then(|bytes| base.checked_add(bytes));
        if self.map_pages.is_some()
            || base == 0
            || base % PAGE_BYTES != 0
            || capacity_pages == 0
            || capacity.is_none()
        {
            return Err(if self.map_pages.is_some() {
                FrameHeapInitError::AlreadyConfigured
            } else {
                FrameHeapInitError::InvalidRange
            });
        }
        self.base = base;
        self.capacity_pages = capacity_pages;
        self.context = context;
        self.map_pages = Some(map_pages);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn contains_pointer(&self, pointer: usize) -> bool {
        self.capacity_pages
            .checked_mul(PAGE_BYTES)
            .and_then(|capacity| self.base.checked_add(capacity).map(|end| (capacity, end)))
            .is_some_and(|(capacity, end)| capacity != 0 && (self.base..end).contains(&pointer))
    }

    fn allocate(&mut self, layout: Layout) -> Result<NonNull<u8>, HeapError> {
        if layout.size() == 0 {
            return Err(HeapError::ZeroSizedAllocation);
        }
        let map_pages = self.map_pages.ok_or(HeapError::OutOfMemory)?;
        let slot = self
            .allocations
            .iter()
            .position(Option::is_none)
            .ok_or(HeapError::AllocationTableFull)?;
        let start = self.find_gap(layout)?;
        let end = start
            .checked_add(layout.size())
            .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
        let required_pages = end
            .checked_add(PAGE_BYTES - 1)
            .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?
            / PAGE_BYTES;
        if required_pages > self.mapped_pages {
            let first_page = self.mapped_pages;
            let page_count = required_pages - first_page;
            // SAFETY: Configuration is unsafe at the public boundary. The
            // mapper contract requires an all-or-nothing mapping of this range.
            if !unsafe { map_pages(self.context, first_page, page_count) } {
                return Err(HeapError::OutOfMemory);
            }
            self.mapped_pages = required_pages;
        }

        self.allocations[slot] = Some(Allocation {
            start,
            size: layout.size(),
            alignment: layout.align(),
        });
        let pointer = self
            .base
            .checked_add(start)
            .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
        NonNull::new(pointer as *mut u8).ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)
    }

    fn deallocate(&mut self, pointer: NonNull<u8>, layout: Layout) -> Result<(), HeapError> {
        if layout.size() == 0 {
            return Err(HeapError::ZeroSizedAllocation);
        }
        let allocation_start = (pointer.as_ptr() as usize)
            .checked_sub(self.base)
            .filter(|offset| *offset < self.capacity_pages.saturating_mul(PAGE_BYTES))
            .ok_or(HeapError::InvalidPointer)?;
        for allocation in &mut self.allocations {
            let Some(active) = *allocation else {
                continue;
            };
            if active.start != allocation_start {
                continue;
            }
            if active.size != layout.size() || active.alignment != layout.align() {
                return Err(HeapError::LayoutMismatch);
            }
            *allocation = None;
            return Ok(());
        }
        Err(HeapError::InvalidPointer)
    }

    fn find_gap(&self, layout: Layout) -> Result<usize, HeapError> {
        let capacity = self
            .capacity_pages
            .checked_mul(PAGE_BYTES)
            .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
        let mut candidate = 0usize;
        loop {
            let candidate_address = self
                .base
                .checked_add(candidate)
                .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
            let aligned_address = candidate_address
                .checked_add(layout.align() - 1)
                .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?
                & !(layout.align() - 1);
            let start = aligned_address
                .checked_sub(self.base)
                .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
            let end = start
                .checked_add(layout.size())
                .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
            if end > capacity {
                return Err(HeapError::OutOfMemory);
            }
            let mut conflicting_end = None;
            for allocation in self.allocations.iter().flatten() {
                let allocation_end = allocation
                    .start
                    .checked_add(allocation.size)
                    .ok_or(HeapError::AddressOverflow)?;
                if start < allocation_end && allocation.start < end {
                    conflicting_end = Some(
                        conflicting_end
                            .map_or(allocation_end, |current: usize| current.max(allocation_end)),
                    );
                }
            }
            match conflicting_end {
                Some(end) => candidate = end,
                None => return Ok(start),
            }
        }
    }
}

const PAGE_BYTES: usize = 4096;

/// Errors reported while installing the optional frame-backed heap region.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum FrameHeapInitError {
    InvalidRange,
    AlreadyConfigured,
}

/// A `GlobalAlloc` wrapper for the fixed bootstrap arena and bounded growth region.
///
/// The bootstrap arena and callback context must remain at stable addresses for
/// the lifetime of allocations. The growth callback must map the complete page
/// range transactionally and must not allocate or call this heap recursively.
pub struct LockedHeap<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> {
    lock: IrqSpinLock<()>,
    heap: UnsafeCell<FixedHeap<HEAP_SIZE, MAX_ALLOCATIONS>>,
    growth: UnsafeCell<FrameBackedHeap<MAX_ALLOCATIONS>>,
}

// SAFETY: `heap` and `growth` are accessed mutably only while the IRQ-save
// spin lock is held. Allocation remains prohibited in interrupt context.
unsafe impl<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> Sync
    for LockedHeap<HEAP_SIZE, MAX_ALLOCATIONS>
{
}

impl<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> LockedHeap<HEAP_SIZE, MAX_ALLOCATIONS> {
    /// Construct an empty allocator. The backing arena is zero-initialized BSS.
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            lock: IrqSpinLock::new(()),
            heap: UnsafeCell::new(FixedHeap::new()),
            growth: UnsafeCell::new(FrameBackedHeap::new()),
        }
    }

    /// Configure one reserved virtual range for demand-mapped heap growth.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// The caller must reserve the complete range exclusively, keep `context`
    /// alive and stable until the allocator is no longer used, and provide a
    /// mapper that atomically maps all requested pages or leaves the range
    /// unchanged. The mapper must not allocate or re-enter this allocator.
    pub unsafe fn initialize_frame_backed_region(
        &self,
        base: usize,
        capacity_pages: usize,
        context: *mut (),
        map_pages: HeapPageMapper,
    ) -> Result<(), FrameHeapInitError> {
        let _lock = self.acquire();
        // SAFETY: The lock grants exclusive access to the growth configuration.
        let growth = unsafe { &mut *self.growth.get() };
        growth.configure(base, capacity_pages, context, map_pages)
    }

    fn acquire(&self) -> IrqSpinLockGuard<'_, ()> {
        self.lock.lock()
    }
}

unsafe impl<const HEAP_SIZE: usize, const MAX_ALLOCATIONS: usize> GlobalAlloc
    for LockedHeap<HEAP_SIZE, MAX_ALLOCATIONS>
{
    unsafe fn alloc(&self, layout: Layout) -> *mut u8 {
        let _lock = self.acquire();
        // SAFETY: The lock grants exclusive access to both allocator regions.
        let heap = unsafe { &mut *self.heap.get() };
        // SAFETY: The same lock exclusively protects the growth metadata and
        // callback configuration. Its mapper contract forbids allocator reentry.
        let growth = unsafe { &mut *self.growth.get() };
        heap.allocate(layout)
            .or_else(|_| growth.allocate(layout))
            .map(NonNull::as_ptr)
            .unwrap_or(core::ptr::null_mut())
    }

    unsafe fn dealloc(&self, pointer: *mut u8, layout: Layout) {
        let Some(pointer) = NonNull::new(pointer) else {
            return;
        };
        let _lock = self.acquire();
        // SAFETY: The lock grants exclusive access to both allocator regions. The
        // GlobalAlloc caller must provide a live allocation and its original layout.
        let heap = unsafe { &mut *self.heap.get() };
        // SAFETY: The same lock exclusively protects growth allocation metadata.
        let growth = unsafe { &mut *self.growth.get() };
        if growth.contains_pointer(pointer.as_ptr() as usize) {
            let _ = growth.deallocate(pointer, layout);
        } else {
            let _ = heap.deallocate(pointer, layout);
        }
    }
}

        let allocation = heap.allocate(layout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(allocation.as_ptr() as usize % layout.align(), 0);

        // SAFETY: The pointer names a live allocation of the requested size.
        unsafe { allocation.as_ptr().write_bytes(0xa5, layout.size()) };
        for index in 0..layout.size() {
            // SAFETY: `index` is bounded by the live allocation's size.
            assert_eq!(unsafe { allocation.as_ptr().add(index).read() }, 0xa5);
        }

        heap.deallocate(allocation, layout).unwrap();
        let reused = heap.allocate(layout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(reused, allocation);
        heap.deallocate(reused, layout).unwrap();
    }

        let mut heap = FixedHeap::<128, 4>::new();
        let full_layout = Layout::from_size_align(64, 1).unwrap();
        let first = heap.allocate(full_layout).unwrap();
        let second = heap.allocate(full_layout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            heap.allocate(Layout::from_size_align(1, 1).unwrap()),
            Err(HeapError::OutOfMemory)
        );

        heap.deallocate(first, full_layout).unwrap();
        let smaller_layout = Layout::from_size_align(32, 1).unwrap();
        let reused = heap.allocate(smaller_layout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(reused, first);
        heap.deallocate(reused, smaller_layout).unwrap();
        heap.deallocate(second, full_layout).unwrap();
    }

        let mut heap = FixedHeap::<128, 1>::new();
        let layout = Layout::from_size_align(8, 1).unwrap();
        let allocation = heap.allocate(layout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(heap.allocate(layout), Err(HeapError::AllocationTableFull));
        heap.deallocate(allocation, layout).unwrap();
        assert!(heap.allocate(layout).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_invalid_pointer_and_layout_without_releasing_memory() {
        let mut heap = FixedHeap::<128, 4>::new();
        let layout = Layout::from_size_align(16, 8).unwrap();
        let allocation = heap.allocate(layout).unwrap();
        let wrong_layout = Layout::from_size_align(8, 8).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            heap.deallocate(allocation, wrong_layout),
            Err(HeapError::LayoutMismatch)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            heap.deallocate(NonNull::dangling(), layout),
            Err(HeapError::InvalidPointer)
        );
        heap.deallocate(allocation, layout).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(

        );

    fn frame_backed_heap_maps_on_demand_and_reuses_freed_allocations() {
        let mut region = TestRegion([0; PAGE_BYTES * 2]);
        let mut trace = MapTrace::default();
        let mut heap = FrameBackedHeap::<4>::new();
        heap.configure(

        assert_eq!(trace.mapped_pages, 2);
        assert_eq!(heap.mapped_pages, 2);
        // SAFETY: The test mapper records a successful mapping of the complete

        unsafe { allocation.as_ptr().add(4999).write(0xa5) };
        // SAFETY: The final byte lies within the live 5000-byte allocation.
        assert_eq!(unsafe { allocation.as_ptr().add(4999).read() }, 0xa5);
        heap.deallocate(allocation, layout).unwrap();

//! Fixed-capacity policy state for single-vCPU kernel threads.
//!
//! This module does not own stacks, switch CPU contexts, or access hardware.
//! Its caller must serialize every call, including against timer IRQs (the
//! runtime does so by disabling local interrupts around policy mutations). A
//! thread is either ready, the sole running thread, blocked on exactly
//! one live wait queue, or exited. Exited slots remain occupied until `reap`.
//! Dispatch scans slots in deterministic round-robin order; waiters are woken
//! in FIFO order. All storage is inline and bounded by the const capacities.

/// Opaque identity for a thread slot allocation.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ThreadId {
    slot: usize,
    generation: u64,
}

impl ThreadId {
    pub const fn slot_index(self) -> usize {
        self.slot
    }
}

/// Build the fresh stack frame consumed by the x86_64 cooperative switch.
///
/// The saved-register order is R15, R14, R13, R12, RBP, RBX, followed by the
/// trampoline return address. The returned address is 16-byte aligned; after
/// six pops and `ret`, the trampoline observes the SysV entry alignment
/// (`RSP % 16 == 8`). This helper only prepares bounded inline stack storage.
pub fn initialize_thread_context_stack(
    stack: &mut [usize],
    saved_registers: [usize; 6],
    trampoline: usize,
) -> Option<usize> {
    const REGISTER_SLOTS: usize = 6;
    const FRAME_SLOTS: usize = REGISTER_SLOTS + 1;
    let word_size = core::mem::size_of::<usize>();
    let frame_bytes = FRAME_SLOTS.checked_mul(word_size)?;
    let stack_bytes = stack.len().checked_mul(word_size)?;
    let stack_start = stack.as_mut_ptr() as usize;
    let stack_end = stack_start.checked_add(stack_bytes)?;
    let frame_start = stack_end.checked_sub(frame_bytes)? & !15usize;
    let frame_offset = frame_start.checked_sub(stack_start)?;
    if frame_offset % word_size != 0 {
        return None;
    }
    let first_slot = frame_offset / word_size;
    let frame_end = first_slot.checked_add(FRAME_SLOTS)?;
    if frame_end > stack.len() || frame_start & 15 != 0 {
        return None;
    }

    stack[first_slot..first_slot + REGISTER_SLOTS].copy_from_slice(&saved_registers);
    stack[first_slot + REGISTER_SLOTS] = trampoline;
    Some(frame_start)
}

/// Opaque identity for a wait-queue allocation.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct WaitQueueId {
    slot: usize,
    generation: u64,
}

/// Lifecycle state of a live thread slot.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ThreadState {
    Ready,
    Running,
    Blocked(WaitQueueId),
    Exited,
}

/// Failures are explicit; rejected operations leave policy state unchanged.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum SchedulerError {
    ThreadCapacityFull,
    WaitQueueCapacityFull,
    WaiterCapacityFull,
    InvalidThread,
    InvalidWaitQueue,
    NoCurrentThread,
    CurrentThreadRunning,
    ThreadNotExited,
    WaitQueueNotEmpty,
    GenerationExhausted,
    InvalidTransition,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct ThreadSlot {
    generation: u64,
    state: Option<ThreadState>,
}

impl ThreadSlot {
    const EMPTY: Self = Self {
        generation: 0,
        state: None,
    };
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct WaitQueue<const WAITERS: usize> {
    generation: u64,
    active: bool,
    waiters: [Option<ThreadId>; WAITERS],
    len: usize,
}

impl<const WAITERS: usize> WaitQueue<WAITERS> {
    const EMPTY: Self = Self {
        generation: 0,
        active: false,
        waiters: [None; WAITERS],
        len: 0,
    };
}

/// Bounded scheduler policy with no allocation or architecture dependencies.
///
/// `THREADS` bounds all live threads, including exited threads not yet reaped;
/// `QUEUES` bounds live wait queues; and `WAITERS` bounds each queue. The
/// scheduler enforces at most one running thread and consistent blocked/queue
/// membership, but its single-owner/single-CPU contract is caller-enforced.
pub struct Scheduler<const THREADS: usize, const QUEUES: usize, const WAITERS: usize> {
    threads: [ThreadSlot; THREADS],
    queues: [WaitQueue<WAITERS>; QUEUES],
    current: Option<ThreadId>,
    next_ready: usize,
}

impl<const THREADS: usize, const QUEUES: usize, const WAITERS: usize>
    Scheduler<THREADS, QUEUES, WAITERS>
{
    /// Create an empty scheduler. Zero capacities are permitted and fail
    /// explicitly when the corresponding resource is requested.
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            threads: [ThreadSlot::EMPTY; THREADS],
            queues: [WaitQueue::EMPTY; QUEUES],
            current: None,
            next_ready: 0,
        }
    }

    /// Add a ready thread, returning its generation-checked slot identity.
    pub fn create_thread(&mut self) -> Result<ThreadId, SchedulerError> {
        let mut generation_exhausted = false;
        for (index, slot) in self.threads.iter_mut().enumerate() {
            if slot.state.is_some() {
                continue;
            }
            let Some(generation) = slot.generation.checked_add(1) else {
                generation_exhausted = true;
                continue;
            };
            slot.generation = generation;
            slot.state = Some(ThreadState::Ready);
            return Ok(ThreadId {
                slot: index,
                generation,
            });
        }
        if generation_exhausted {
            Err(SchedulerError::GenerationExhausted)
        } else {
            Err(SchedulerError::ThreadCapacityFull)
        }
    }

    /// Current running thread, if any.
    pub const fn current(&self) -> Option<ThreadId> {
        self.current
    }

    /// Query a live thread's lifecycle state. Stale and unknown IDs are rejected.
    pub fn state(&self, thread: ThreadId) -> Result<ThreadState, SchedulerError> {
        let slot = self.thread_slot(thread)?;
        slot.state.ok_or(SchedulerError::InvalidThread)
    }

    /// Select the next ready thread when the CPU has no running thread.
    pub fn dispatch(&mut self) -> Result<Option<ThreadId>, SchedulerError> {
        if self.current.is_some() {
            return Err(SchedulerError::CurrentThreadRunning);
        }
        Ok(self.select_ready())
    }

    /// Cooperatively yield the running thread and dispatch the next ready one.
    pub fn yield_current(&mut self) -> Result<ThreadId, SchedulerError> {
        self.preempt_current()
    }

    /// Put the running thread at the end of the round-robin turn and select the
    /// next ready thread. Timer-driven preemption uses the same policy transition.
    pub fn preempt_current(&mut self) -> Result<ThreadId, SchedulerError> {
        let current = self.current.ok_or(SchedulerError::NoCurrentThread)?;
        let slot = self.thread_slot_mut(current)?;
        if slot.state != Some(ThreadState::Running) {
            return Err(SchedulerError::InvalidTransition);
        }
        slot.state = Some(ThreadState::Ready);
        self.current = None;
        self.select_ready().ok_or(SchedulerError::InvalidTransition)
    }

    /// Exit the running thread and dispatch another ready thread, if one exists.
    /// The exited slot remains unavailable until explicitly reaped.
    pub fn exit_current(&mut self) -> Result<Option<ThreadId>, SchedulerError> {
        let current = self.current.ok_or(SchedulerError::NoCurrentThread)?;
        let slot = self.thread_slot_mut(current)?;
        if slot.state != Some(ThreadState::Running) {
            return Err(SchedulerError::InvalidTransition);
        }
        slot.state = Some(ThreadState::Exited);
        self.current = None;
        Ok(self.select_ready())
    }

    /// Release an exited thread slot so it can be reused with a new ID.
    pub fn reap(&mut self, thread: ThreadId) -> Result<(), SchedulerError> {
        let slot = self.thread_slot_mut(thread)?;
        if slot.state != Some(ThreadState::Exited) {
            return Err(SchedulerError::ThreadNotExited);
        }
        slot.state = None;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Create an empty bounded wait queue.
    pub fn create_wait_queue(&mut self) -> Result<WaitQueueId, SchedulerError> {
        let mut generation_exhausted = false;
        for (index, queue) in self.queues.iter_mut().enumerate() {
            if queue.active {
                continue;
            }
            let Some(generation) = queue.generation.checked_add(1) else {
                generation_exhausted = true;
                continue;
            };
            queue.generation = generation;
            queue.active = true;
            queue.len = 0;
            queue.waiters.fill(None);
            return Ok(WaitQueueId {
                slot: index,
                generation,
            });
        }
        if generation_exhausted {
            Err(SchedulerError::GenerationExhausted)
        } else {
            Err(SchedulerError::WaitQueueCapacityFull)
        }
    }

    /// Destroy an empty queue. A queue with sleepers cannot be destroyed.
    pub fn destroy_wait_queue(&mut self, queue: WaitQueueId) -> Result<(), SchedulerError> {
        let queue = self.queue_slot_mut(queue)?;
        if queue.len != 0 {
            return Err(SchedulerError::WaitQueueNotEmpty);
        }
        queue.active = false;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Block the running thread on a queue, then dispatch another ready thread.
    /// A full or invalid queue leaves the current thread running.
    pub fn sleep_current(
        &mut self,
        queue_id: WaitQueueId,
    ) -> Result<Option<ThreadId>, SchedulerError> {
        let queue = self.queue_slot(queue_id)?;
        if queue.len == WAITERS {
            return Err(SchedulerError::WaiterCapacityFull);
        }
        let current = self.current.ok_or(SchedulerError::NoCurrentThread)?;
        let thread = self.thread_slot(current)?;
        if thread.state != Some(ThreadState::Running) {
            return Err(SchedulerError::InvalidTransition);
        }

        let queue = &mut self.queues[queue_id.slot];
        queue.waiters[queue.len] = Some(current);
        queue.len += 1;
        self.threads[current.slot].state = Some(ThreadState::Blocked(queue_id));
        self.current = None;
        Ok(self.select_ready())
    }

    /// Wake the oldest waiter, making it ready but not preempting the current
    /// thread. Returns `None` when the valid queue has no waiters.
    pub fn wake_one(&mut self, queue_id: WaitQueueId) -> Result<Option<ThreadId>, SchedulerError> {
        let queue = self.queue_slot(queue_id)?;
        if queue.len == 0 {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let thread_id = queue.waiters[0].ok_or(SchedulerError::InvalidTransition)?;
        let thread = self.thread_slot(thread_id)?;
        if thread.state != Some(ThreadState::Blocked(queue_id)) {
            return Err(SchedulerError::InvalidTransition);
        }

        let queue = &mut self.queues[queue_id.slot];
        for index in 1..queue.len {
            queue.waiters[index - 1] = queue.waiters[index];
        }
        queue.len -= 1;
        queue.waiters[queue.len] = None;
        self.threads[thread_id.slot].state = Some(ThreadState::Ready);
        Ok(Some(thread_id))
    }

    /// Wake every waiter in FIFO order, making them ready without preemption.
    pub fn wake_all(&mut self, queue_id: WaitQueueId) -> Result<usize, SchedulerError> {
        let queue = self.queue_slot(queue_id)?;
        let count = queue.len;

        for waiter in queue.waiters[..count].iter().flatten() {
            let thread = self.thread_slot(*waiter)?;
            if thread.state != Some(ThreadState::Blocked(queue_id)) {
                return Err(SchedulerError::InvalidTransition);
            }
        }

        for waiter in self.queues[queue_id.slot].waiters[..count].iter().flatten() {
            self.threads[waiter.slot].state = Some(ThreadState::Ready);
        }
        let queue = &mut self.queues[queue_id.slot];
        queue.waiters.fill(None);
        queue.len = 0;
        Ok(count)
    }

    fn select_ready(&mut self) -> Option<ThreadId> {
        if THREADS == 0 {
            return None;
        }
        for offset in 0..THREADS {
            let index = (self.next_ready + offset) % THREADS;
            if self.threads[index].state == Some(ThreadState::Ready) {
                let thread = ThreadId {
                    slot: index,
                    generation: self.threads[index].generation,
                };
                self.threads[index].state = Some(ThreadState::Running);
                self.current = Some(thread);
                self.next_ready = (index + 1) % THREADS;
                return Some(thread);
            }
        }
        None
    }

    fn thread_slot(&self, thread: ThreadId) -> Result<&ThreadSlot, SchedulerError> {
        self.threads
            .get(thread.slot)
            .filter(|slot| slot.generation == thread.generation && slot.state.is_some())
            .ok_or(SchedulerError::InvalidThread)
    }

    fn thread_slot_mut(&mut self, thread: ThreadId) -> Result<&mut ThreadSlot, SchedulerError> {
        self.threads
            .get_mut(thread.slot)
            .filter(|slot| slot.generation == thread.generation && slot.state.is_some())
            .ok_or(SchedulerError::InvalidThread)
    }

    fn queue_slot(&self, queue: WaitQueueId) -> Result<&WaitQueue<WAITERS>, SchedulerError> {
        self.queues
            .get(queue.slot)
            .filter(|slot| slot.active && slot.generation == queue.generation)
            .ok_or(SchedulerError::InvalidWaitQueue)
    }

    fn queue_slot_mut(
        &mut self,
        queue: WaitQueueId,
    ) -> Result<&mut WaitQueue<WAITERS>, SchedulerError> {
        self.queues
            .get_mut(queue.slot)
            .filter(|slot| slot.active && slot.generation == queue.generation)
            .ok_or(SchedulerError::InvalidWaitQueue)
    }
}

impl<const THREADS: usize, const QUEUES: usize, const WAITERS: usize> Default
    for Scheduler<THREADS, QUEUES, WAITERS>
{
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::{initialize_thread_context_stack, Scheduler, SchedulerError, ThreadState};
    use core::assert_eq;

    type TestScheduler = Scheduler<3, 2, 2>;

    #[test]
    fn fresh_context_frame_has_sysv_alignment_and_saved_register_order() {
        let mut stack = [0usize; 32];
        let registers = [15, 14, 13, 12, 5, 3];
        let trampoline = 0x1234_5678usize;
        let rsp = initialize_thread_context_stack(&mut stack, registers, trampoline).unwrap();
        let first_slot = (rsp - stack.as_ptr() as usize) / core::mem::size_of::<usize>();

        assert_eq!(rsp & 15, 0);
        assert_eq!((rsp + 7 * core::mem::size_of::<usize>()) & 15, 8);
        assert_eq!(&stack[first_slot..first_slot + 6], &registers);
        assert_eq!(stack[first_slot + 6], trampoline);
    }

    #[test]
    fn fresh_context_frame_rejects_insufficient_stack_without_writing() {
        let mut stack = [usize::MAX; 6];
        assert_eq!(
            initialize_thread_context_stack(&mut stack, [0; 6], 0x1234),
            None
        );
        assert_eq!(stack, [usize::MAX; 6]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn round_robin_dispatch_yield_and_exit_follow_lifecycle() {
        let mut scheduler = TestScheduler::new();
        let first = scheduler.create_thread().unwrap();
        let second = scheduler.create_thread().unwrap();
        let third = scheduler.create_thread().unwrap();

        assert_eq!(scheduler.state(first), Ok(ThreadState::Ready));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.dispatch(), Ok(Some(first)));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.current(), Some(first));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.state(first), Ok(ThreadState::Running));
        assert_eq!(
            scheduler.dispatch(),
            Err(SchedulerError::CurrentThreadRunning)
        );

        assert_eq!(scheduler.yield_current(), Ok(second));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.state(first), Ok(ThreadState::Ready));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.yield_current(), Ok(third));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.exit_current(), Ok(Some(first)));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.state(third), Ok(ThreadState::Exited));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.reap(third), Ok(()));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.state(third), Err(SchedulerError::InvalidThread));

        let replacement = scheduler.create_thread().unwrap();
        assert_ne!(replacement, third);
        assert_eq!(scheduler.state(replacement), Ok(ThreadState::Ready));
    }

    #[test]
    fn timer_preemption_rotates_running_thread_and_keeps_both_ready() {
        let mut scheduler = TestScheduler::new();
        let first = scheduler.create_thread().unwrap();
        let second = scheduler.create_thread().unwrap();

        assert_eq!(scheduler.dispatch(), Ok(Some(first)));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.preempt_current(), Ok(second));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.state(first), Ok(ThreadState::Ready));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.state(second), Ok(ThreadState::Running));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.preempt_current(), Ok(first));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.state(second), Ok(ThreadState::Ready));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.state(first), Ok(ThreadState::Running));
    }

    #[test]
    fn final_thread_can_yield_to_itself_and_exit_to_idle() {
        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::<1, 0, 0>::new();
        let only = scheduler.create_thread().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(scheduler.dispatch(), Ok(Some(only)));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.yield_current(), Ok(only));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.exit_current(), Ok(None));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.current(), None);
        assert_eq!(scheduler.dispatch(), Ok(None));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.reap(only), Ok(()));
    }

    #[test]
    fn queues_wake_in_fifo_order_and_do_not_preempt() {
        let mut scheduler = TestScheduler::new();
        let queue = scheduler.create_wait_queue().unwrap();
        let first = scheduler.create_thread().unwrap();
        let second = scheduler.create_thread().unwrap();
        let third = scheduler.create_thread().unwrap();

        assert_eq!(scheduler.dispatch(), Ok(Some(first)));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.sleep_current(queue), Ok(Some(second)));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.state(first), Ok(ThreadState::Blocked(queue)));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.sleep_current(queue), Ok(Some(third)));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.state(second), Ok(ThreadState::Blocked(queue)));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.wake_one(queue), Ok(Some(first)));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.current(), Some(third));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.state(first), Ok(ThreadState::Ready));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.wake_one(queue), Ok(Some(second)));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.wake_one(queue), Ok(None));

        assert_eq!(scheduler.exit_current(), Ok(Some(first)));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.exit_current(), Ok(Some(second)));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.exit_current(), Ok(None));
    }

    #[test]
    fn wake_all_makes_every_waiter_ready_and_queue_can_be_reused() {
        let mut scheduler = TestScheduler::new();
        let queue = scheduler.create_wait_queue().unwrap();
        let a = scheduler.create_thread().unwrap();
        let b = scheduler.create_thread().unwrap();
        let c = scheduler.create_thread().unwrap();

        scheduler.dispatch().unwrap();
        scheduler.sleep_current(queue).unwrap();
        scheduler.sleep_current(queue).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(scheduler.wake_all(queue), Ok(2));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.state(a), Ok(ThreadState::Ready));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.state(b), Ok(ThreadState::Ready));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.state(c), Ok(ThreadState::Running));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.wake_all(queue), Ok(0));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.destroy_wait_queue(queue), Ok(()));

        let reused = scheduler.create_wait_queue().unwrap();
        assert_ne!(queue, reused);
        assert_eq!(
            scheduler.wake_one(queue),
            Err(SchedulerError::InvalidWaitQueue)
        );
        assert_eq!(scheduler.wake_one(reused), Ok(None));
    }

    #[test]
    fn capacity_and_invalid_operations_are_explicit_and_non_mutating() {
        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::<1, 1, 1>::new();
        assert_eq!(
            scheduler.yield_current(),
            Err(SchedulerError::NoCurrentThread)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            scheduler.exit_current(),
            Err(SchedulerError::NoCurrentThread)
        );

        let queue = scheduler.create_wait_queue().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            scheduler.create_wait_queue(),
            Err(SchedulerError::WaitQueueCapacityFull)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            scheduler.sleep_current(queue),
            Err(SchedulerError::NoCurrentThread)
        );
        let thread = scheduler.create_thread().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            scheduler.create_thread(),
            Err(SchedulerError::ThreadCapacityFull)
        );
        assert_eq!(scheduler.reap(thread), Err(SchedulerError::ThreadNotExited));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.state(thread), Ok(ThreadState::Ready));

        scheduler.dispatch().unwrap();
        scheduler.sleep_current(queue).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            scheduler.destroy_wait_queue(queue),
            Err(SchedulerError::WaitQueueNotEmpty)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            scheduler.create_thread(),
            Err(SchedulerError::ThreadCapacityFull)
        );
        assert_eq!(scheduler.wake_one(queue), Ok(Some(thread)));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.state(thread), Ok(ThreadState::Ready));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.dispatch(), Ok(Some(thread)));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.exit_current(), Ok(None));
        scheduler.reap(thread).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(scheduler.destroy_wait_queue(queue), Ok(()));
    }

    #[test]
    fn full_queue_rejects_sleep_without_blocking_the_running_thread() {
        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::<2, 1, 1>::new();
        let queue = scheduler.create_wait_queue().unwrap();
        let first = scheduler.create_thread().unwrap();
        let second = scheduler.create_thread().unwrap();

        scheduler.dispatch().unwrap();
        scheduler.sleep_current(queue).unwrap();
        let current_before = scheduler.current();
        assert_eq!(
            scheduler.sleep_current(queue),
            Err(SchedulerError::WaiterCapacityFull)
        );
        assert_eq!(scheduler.current(), current_before);
        assert_eq!(scheduler.state(second), Ok(ThreadState::Running));
        assert_eq!(scheduler.state(first), Ok(ThreadState::Blocked(queue)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn stale_thread_and_queue_handles_are_rejected_after_reuse() {
        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::<1, 1, 1>::new();
        let old_thread = scheduler.create_thread().unwrap();
        scheduler.dispatch().unwrap();
        scheduler.exit_current().unwrap();
        scheduler.reap(old_thread).unwrap();
        let new_thread = scheduler.create_thread().unwrap();
        assert_ne!(old_thread, new_thread);
        assert_eq!(
            scheduler.state(old_thread),
            Err(SchedulerError::InvalidThread)
        );

        let old_queue = scheduler.create_wait_queue().unwrap();
        scheduler.destroy_wait_queue(old_queue).unwrap();
        let new_queue = scheduler.create_wait_queue().unwrap();
        assert_ne!(old_queue, new_queue);
        assert_eq!(
            scheduler.wake_one(old_queue),
            Err(SchedulerError::InvalidWaitQueue)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn zero_capacities_are_valid_and_report_exhaustion() {
        let mut scheduler = Scheduler::<0, 0, 0>::new();
        assert_eq!(scheduler.dispatch(), Ok(None));
        assert_eq!(
            scheduler.create_thread(),
            Err(SchedulerError::ThreadCapacityFull)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            scheduler.create_wait_queue(),
            Err(SchedulerError::WaitQueueCapacityFull)
        );
    }
}

//! Fixed-capacity single-vCPU kernel-thread runtime and scheduling smoke tests.
//!
//! Thread stacks are allocator-owned 4 KiB mappings with one unmapped lower
//! guard page. Scheduler state is mutated only with local interrupts disabled.
//! The PIT handler may preempt a running thread by suspending its own call stack
//! on that thread's kernel stack and switching to another saved context.

use crate::kprintln;
use core::arch::asm;
use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicPtr, AtomicUsize, Ordering};
use rustix_kernel::frame::{Frame, FrameAllocator};

use rustix_kernel::paging::{
    validate_mapping_range, CachePolicy, CandidatePageTableMemory, CandidatePageTables,
    EffectiveMemoryType, MtrrState, PagePermissions, PageWalkOutcome, PatLayout, PAGE_SIZE,
};
use rustix_kernel::scheduler::{
    initialize_thread_context_stack, Scheduler, SchedulerError, ThreadId, ThreadState, WaitQueueId,
};
use rustix_kernel::time::AtomicTickCounter;

const MAX_THREADS: usize = 2;
const THREAD_STACK_PAGES: usize = 4;
const THREAD_STACK_STRIDE: u64 = (THREAD_STACK_PAGES as u64 + 1) * PAGE_SIZE;
const THREAD_STACK_VIRTUAL_BASE: u64 = 0xffff_c400_0000_0000;
const CONTEXT_COUNT: usize = MAX_THREADS + 1;
const QUEUE_COUNT: usize = MAX_THREADS + 1;
const _: [(); QUEUE_COUNT] = [(); MAX_THREADS + 1];

static THREAD_TEST_TRACE: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);
static ACTIVE_RUNTIME: AtomicPtr<KernelThreadRuntime> = AtomicPtr::new(core::ptr::null_mut());

#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
static PREEMPTION_A_STARTED: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);
#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
static PREEMPTION_B_STARTED: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);
#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
static PREEMPTION_TEST_FAILED: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);
#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
const PREEMPTION_TEST_TICK_BUDGET: u64 = 8;

type ThreadEntry = extern "C" fn(*mut (), usize);

struct KernelThreadRuntime {
    policy: Scheduler<MAX_THREADS, QUEUE_COUNT, MAX_THREADS>,
    saved_rsp: [usize; CONTEXT_COUNT],
    thread_ids: [Option<ThreadId>; MAX_THREADS],
    stack_virtual_starts: [Option<u64>; MAX_THREADS],
    entries: [Option<ThreadEntry>; MAX_THREADS],
    arguments: [usize; MAX_THREADS],
    deadlines: [Option<u64>; MAX_THREADS],
    event_queue: WaitQueueId,
    timer_queues: [WaitQueueId; MAX_THREADS],
    current_context: usize,
    input_events_enabled: bool,
    ticks: &'static AtomicTickCounter,
}

impl KernelThreadRuntime {
    fn new(ticks: &'static AtomicTickCounter) -> Result<Self, SchedulerError> {
        let mut policy = Scheduler::new();
        let event_queue = policy.create_wait_queue()?;
        let mut timer_queues = [event_queue; MAX_THREADS];
        for queue in &mut timer_queues {
            *queue = policy.create_wait_queue()?;
        }
        Ok(Self {
            policy,
            saved_rsp: [0; CONTEXT_COUNT],
            thread_ids: [None; MAX_THREADS],
            stack_virtual_starts: [None; MAX_THREADS],
            entries: [None; MAX_THREADS],
            arguments: [0; MAX_THREADS],
            deadlines: [None; MAX_THREADS],
            event_queue,
            timer_queues,
            current_context: 0,
            input_events_enabled: false,
            ticks,
        })
    }

    fn all_threads_exited(&self) -> bool {
        self.thread_ids
            .iter()
            .flatten()
            .all(|thread| self.policy.state(*thread) == Ok(ThreadState::Exited))
    }

    fn wake_expired(&mut self) {
        let now = self.ticks.ticks();
        for slot in 0..MAX_THREADS {
            if self.deadlines[slot].is_some_and(|deadline| now >= deadline) {
                self.deadlines[slot] = None;
                if self.policy.wake_one(self.timer_queues[slot]).is_err() {
                    THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(99, Ordering::Release);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    fn wake_ready_events(&mut self) {
        self.wake_expired();
        if self.input_events_enabled
            && rustix_kernel::input::INPUT_EVENT_PENDING.swap(false, Ordering::AcqRel)
            && self.policy.wake_all(self.event_queue).is_err()
        {
            THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(99, Ordering::Release);
        }
    }

    unsafe fn run_from_raw(runtime_pointer: *mut Self) {
        let initial_flags = disable_interrupts();
        if ACTIVE_RUNTIME
            .compare_exchange(
                core::ptr::null_mut(),
                runtime_pointer,
                Ordering::Release,
                Ordering::Relaxed,
            )
            .is_err()
        {
            halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure();
        }
        let first = {
            // SAFETY: The caller supplies the live, exclusively owned runtime;
            // the temporary reference ends before the context switch.
            let runtime = unsafe { &mut *runtime_pointer };
            match runtime.policy.dispatch() {
                Ok(Some(thread)) => {
                    let context = thread.slot_index() + 1;
                    runtime.current_context = context;
                    Some(runtime.saved_rsp[context])
                }
                Ok(None) => None,
                Err(_) => {
                    THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(99, Ordering::Release);
                    None
                }
            }
        };
        if let Some(new_rsp) = first {
            // SAFETY: Context zero is the active bootstrap stack; `new_rsp` is a
            // synthetic, ABI-aligned frame on a mapped owned thread stack.
            unsafe {
                rustix_arch_context_switch(
                    core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*runtime_pointer).saved_rsp[0]),
                    new_rsp as *mut usize,
                );
            }
        }
        restore_interrupts(initial_flags);

        loop {
            let flags = disable_interrupts();
            let (new_rsp, finished) = {
                // SAFETY: No other thread runs while IF is clear. All mutable
                // scheduler borrows end before any subsequent context switch.
                let runtime = unsafe { &mut *runtime_pointer };
                runtime.wake_ready_events();
                if runtime.all_threads_exited() {
                    (None, true)
                } else {
                    match runtime.policy.dispatch() {
                        Ok(Some(thread)) => {
                            let context = thread.slot_index() + 1;
                            runtime.current_context = context;
                            (Some(runtime.saved_rsp[context]), false)
                        }
                        Ok(None) => (None, false),
                        Err(_) => {
                            THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(99, Ordering::Release);
                            (None, true)
                        }
                    }
                }
            };
            if finished {
                ACTIVE_RUNTIME.store(core::ptr::null_mut(), Ordering::Release);
                restore_interrupts(flags);
                return;
            }
            if let Some(new_rsp) = new_rsp {
                // SAFETY: The bootstrap context is currently active and the
                // selected thread owns a live saved stack frame.
                unsafe {
                    rustix_arch_context_switch(
                        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*runtime_pointer).saved_rsp[0]),
                        new_rsp as *mut usize,
                    );
                }
                restore_interrupts(flags);
            } else {
                // `sti; hlt` is atomic with respect to the interrupt shadow, so
                // a PIT wakeup cannot be lost between checking deadlines and halt.
                // SAFETY: The verified PIT handler is installed and the only
                // unmasked device route; it performs no allocation or scheduling.
                unsafe { asm!("sti; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Run a single long-lived cooperative worker on an owned guarded stack.
pub fn run_shell<M: CandidatePageTableMemory>(
    candidate: &mut CandidatePageTables<'_, M>,
    allocator: *mut FrameAllocator,
    cpu_info: &crate::arch::x86_64::cpu::CpuInfo,
    ticks: &'static AtomicTickCounter,
    entry: extern "C" fn(*mut (), usize),
    argument: usize,
) -> ! {
    let mut runtime =
        KernelThreadRuntime::new(ticks).unwrap_or_else(|_| halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure());
    runtime.input_events_enabled = true;
    let runtime_pointer = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(runtime);
    let flags = disable_interrupts();
    // SAFETY: The caller supplies the live allocator retained by BootInfo. This
    // exclusive borrow is limited to stack setup and ends before context switches.
    let spawned = unsafe {
        spawn_thread(
            &mut runtime,
            candidate,
            &mut *allocator,
            cpu_info,
            runtime_pointer,
            entry,
            argument,
        )
    };
    if spawned.is_err() {
        restore_interrupts(flags);
        halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure();
    }
    restore_interrupts(flags);
    // SAFETY: The caller keeps the active root, allocator, CPU snapshot, thread
    // context, and callback argument alive for this non-returning kernel runtime.
    unsafe { KernelThreadRuntime::run_from_raw(runtime_pointer) };
    let flags = disable_interrupts();
    // SAFETY: No worker is running after `run_from_raw` returns, so the raw
    // allocator pointer is exclusively available for final stack cleanup.
    let allocator = unsafe { &mut *allocator };
    reap_exited_stacks(&mut runtime, candidate, allocator);
    restore_interrupts(flags);
    halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure()
}

/// Block the current cooperative thread until an input IRQ publishes an event.
pub(crate) fn wait_for_input(runtime_pointer: *mut ()) {
    // SAFETY: Only a normal cooperative thread calls this; IRQ handlers merely
    // publish the atomic event and never touch scheduler policy state.
    if !unsafe { block_current(runtime_pointer.cast(), None) } {
        THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(99, Ordering::Release);
    }
}

/// Exercise real switching, stack guards, event wakeup, timed sleep, and timer preemption.
/// The caller must provide the current active root, keep this single-vCPU kernel
/// path alive for the call, and have already enabled the verified PIT route.
#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
pub fn smoke<M: CandidatePageTableMemory>(
    candidate: &mut CandidatePageTables<'_, M>,
    allocator: &mut FrameAllocator,
    cpu_info: &crate::arch::x86_64::cpu::CpuInfo,
    ticks: &'static AtomicTickCounter,
) -> Result<(), &'static str> {
    THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(0, Ordering::Release);
    let mut runtime = KernelThreadRuntime::new(ticks).map_err(|_| "scheduler setup failed")?;
    let runtime_pointer = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(runtime);

    let flags = disable_interrupts();
    let first = spawn_thread(
        &mut runtime,
        candidate,
        allocator,
        cpu_info,
        runtime_pointer,
        waiter_thread,
        0,
    );
    let second = if first.is_ok() {
        spawn_thread(
            &mut runtime,
            candidate,
            allocator,
            cpu_info,
            runtime_pointer,
            signaler_thread,
            0,
        )
    } else {
        Err("waiter thread stack setup failed")
    };
    restore_interrupts(flags);

    if first.is_err() || second.is_err() {
        cancel_unstarted_threads(&mut runtime);
        let flags = disable_interrupts();
        reap_exited_stacks(&mut runtime, candidate, allocator);
        restore_interrupts(flags);
        return Err(first
            .err()
            .or(second.err())
            .unwrap_or("thread setup failed"));
    }

    // Every stack slot was checked page by page during setup: the lower guard is
    // absent, and all four stack leaves are supervisor RW/NX with the selected WB type.
    kprintln!("kernel thread stacks verified: mapped RW/NX with absent lower guards");
    // SAFETY: The runtime remains on the bootstrap stack and is passed by raw
    // pointer; no mutable reference is retained across the context switches.
    unsafe { KernelThreadRuntime::run_from_raw(runtime_pointer) };

    let passed = THREAD_TEST_TRACE.load(Ordering::Acquire) == 5
        && ticks.ticks() >= 2
        && runtime.all_threads_exited();
    let flags = disable_interrupts();
    reap_exited_stacks(&mut runtime, candidate, allocator);
    restore_interrupts(flags);
    if !passed {
        return Err("cooperative yield/wakeup/timed-sleep sequence failed");
    }
    kprintln!("cooperative thread path passed: yield, event wakeup, timed sleep, stack guards");
    timer_preemption_smoke(candidate, allocator, cpu_info, ticks)
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
fn timer_preemption_smoke<M: CandidatePageTableMemory>(
    candidate: &mut CandidatePageTables<'_, M>,
    allocator: &mut FrameAllocator,
    cpu_info: &crate::arch::x86_64::cpu::CpuInfo,
    ticks: &'static AtomicTickCounter,
) -> Result<(), &'static str> {
    PREEMPTION_A_STARTED.store(0, Ordering::Release);
    PREEMPTION_B_STARTED.store(0, Ordering::Release);
    PREEMPTION_TEST_FAILED.store(0, Ordering::Release);

    let mut runtime =
        KernelThreadRuntime::new(ticks).map_err(|_| "preemption scheduler setup failed")?;
    let runtime_pointer = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(runtime);
    let ticks_pointer = ticks as *const AtomicTickCounter as usize;

    let flags = disable_interrupts();
    let first = spawn_thread(
        &mut runtime,
        candidate,
        allocator,
        cpu_info,
        runtime_pointer,
        non_yielding_preemption_worker_a,
        ticks_pointer,
    );
    let second = if first.is_ok() {
        spawn_thread(
            &mut runtime,
            candidate,
            allocator,
            cpu_info,
            runtime_pointer,
            non_yielding_preemption_worker_b,
            ticks_pointer,
        )
    } else {
        Err("first preemption worker stack setup failed")
    };
    restore_interrupts(flags);

    if first.is_err() || second.is_err() {
        cancel_unstarted_threads(&mut runtime);
        let flags = disable_interrupts();
        reap_exited_stacks(&mut runtime, candidate, allocator);
        restore_interrupts(flags);
        return Err(first
            .err()
            .or(second.err())
            .unwrap_or("preemption worker setup failed"));
    }

    // Both workers busy-wait without yielding. Worker B can start only after a
    // PIT interrupt preempts worker A and dispatches the second saved context.
    unsafe { KernelThreadRuntime::run_from_raw(runtime_pointer) };
    let passed = PREEMPTION_A_STARTED.load(Ordering::Acquire) == 1
        && PREEMPTION_B_STARTED.load(Ordering::Acquire) == 1
        && PREEMPTION_TEST_FAILED.load(Ordering::Acquire) == 0
        && runtime.all_threads_exited();
    let flags = disable_interrupts();
    reap_exited_stacks(&mut runtime, candidate, allocator);
    restore_interrupts(flags);
    if !passed {
        return Err("timer did not preempt a non-yielding thread within the tick budget");
    }
    kprintln!("timer preemption path passed: non-yielding workers both ran");
    Ok(())
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
extern "C" fn non_yielding_preemption_worker_a(_runtime: *mut (), ticks_pointer: usize) {
    PREEMPTION_A_STARTED.store(1, Ordering::Release);
    let ticks = unsafe { &*(ticks_pointer as *const AtomicTickCounter) };
    let deadline = ticks.ticks().saturating_add(PREEMPTION_TEST_TICK_BUDGET);
    while PREEMPTION_B_STARTED.load(Ordering::Acquire) == 0 {
        if ticks.ticks() >= deadline {
            PREEMPTION_TEST_FAILED.store(1, Ordering::Release);
            return;
        }
        spin_loop();
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
extern "C" fn non_yielding_preemption_worker_b(_runtime: *mut (), _ticks_pointer: usize) {
    PREEMPTION_B_STARTED.store(1, Ordering::Release);
}

fn spawn_thread<M: CandidatePageTableMemory>(
    runtime: &mut KernelThreadRuntime,
    candidate: &mut CandidatePageTables<'_, M>,
    allocator: &mut FrameAllocator,
    cpu_info: &crate::arch::x86_64::cpu::CpuInfo,
    runtime_pointer: *mut KernelThreadRuntime,
    entry: ThreadEntry,
    argument: usize,
) -> Result<ThreadId, &'static str> {
    let slot = runtime
        .thread_ids
        .iter()
        .position(Option::is_none)
        .ok_or("thread capacity exhausted")?;
    let region_start = THREAD_STACK_VIRTUAL_BASE
        .checked_add(
            (slot as u64)
                .checked_mul(THREAD_STACK_STRIDE)
                .ok_or("stack VA overflow")?,
        )
        .ok_or("stack VA overflow")?;
    let stack_start = region_start
        .checked_add(PAGE_SIZE)
        .ok_or("stack VA overflow")?;

    for page in 0..=THREAD_STACK_PAGES {
        let address = region_start + page as u64 * PAGE_SIZE;
        if !matches!(
            candidate.walk(address),
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { .. })
        ) {
            return Err("thread guard or stack VA is already mapped");
        }
    }

    let physical_width = cpu_info
        .physical_address_bits
        .ok_or("physical width unavailable")?;
    let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(cpu_info.pat_msr_value.ok_or("PAT unavailable")?)
        .map_err(|_| "PAT state invalid")?;
    let mtrrs = match &cpu_info.mtrr {
        MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers
            .validated_layout(physical_width)
            .map_err(|_| "MTRR state invalid")?,
        _ => return Err("MTRR state unavailable"),
    };
    let permissions = PagePermissions {
        writable: true,
        executable: false,
        user_accessible: false,
    };
    let mut mapped_pages = 0usize;
    for page in 0..THREAD_STACK_PAGES {
        let virtual_address = stack_start + page as u64 * PAGE_SIZE;
        let frame = allocator.allocate().ok_or_else(|| {
            rollback_stack(candidate, allocator, stack_start, mapped_pages);
            "physical frames exhausted for thread stack"
        })?;
        let mapping = match validate_mapping_range(
            virtual_address,
            frame.address(),
            PAGE_SIZE,
            permissions,
            Some(physical_width),
            cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        ) {
            Ok(mapping) => mapping,
            Err(_) => {
                deallocate_or_halt(allocator, frame);
                rollback_stack(candidate, allocator, stack_start, mapped_pages);
                return Err("thread stack mapping rejected");
            }
        };
        let attributes = match mapping.select_cache_attributes(
            CachePolicy::WriteBack,
            pat,
            &mtrrs,
            cpu_info.normal_caching,
        ) {
            Ok(attributes) if attributes.effective_type() == EffectiveMemoryType::WriteBack => {
                attributes
            }
            _ => {
                deallocate_or_halt(allocator, frame);
                rollback_stack(candidate, allocator, stack_start, mapped_pages);
                return Err("thread stack has no uniform write-back policy");
            }
        };
        // SAFETY: The active root is current on this single CPU; IF is clear
        // throughout stack setup, and each mapping uses an allocator-owned frame.
        if let Err(failure) =
            unsafe { candidate.map_owned_page_active(allocator, frame, mapping, attributes) }
        {
            deallocate_or_halt(allocator, failure.frame);
            rollback_stack(candidate, allocator, stack_start, mapped_pages);
            return Err("thread stack mapping failed");
        }
        match candidate.walk(virtual_address) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation))
                if translation.permissions == permissions
                    && translation.pat_index == attributes.pat_index() => {}
            _ => {
                rollback_stack(candidate, allocator, stack_start, mapped_pages + 1);
                return Err("thread stack page-table verification failed");
            }
        }
        mapped_pages += 1;
    }

    let stack_top = stack_start + THREAD_STACK_PAGES as u64 * PAGE_SIZE;
    let frame_word_count = 16;
    let frame_words = unsafe {
        core::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(
            (stack_top as *mut usize).sub(frame_word_count),
            frame_word_count,
        )
    };
    let registers = [0, slot, runtime_pointer as usize, 0, 0, 0];
    let saved_rsp = initialize_thread_context_stack(
        frame_words,
        registers,
        kernel_thread_trampoline as *const () as usize,
    );
    let Some(saved_rsp) = saved_rsp else {
        rollback_stack(candidate, allocator, stack_start, mapped_pages);
        return Err("thread initial context frame did not fit");
    };
    let thread = match runtime.policy.create_thread() {
        Ok(thread) if thread.slot_index() == slot => thread,
        Ok(_) => {
            rollback_stack(candidate, allocator, stack_start, mapped_pages);
            return Err("scheduler slot and stack slot diverged");
        }
        Err(_) => {
            rollback_stack(candidate, allocator, stack_start, mapped_pages);
            return Err("scheduler thread capacity exhausted");
        }
    };
    runtime.thread_ids[slot] = Some(thread);
    runtime.stack_virtual_starts[slot] = Some(stack_start);
    runtime.entries[slot] = Some(entry);
    runtime.arguments[slot] = argument;
    runtime.saved_rsp[slot + 1] = saved_rsp;
    Ok(thread)
}

fn rollback_stack<M: CandidatePageTableMemory>(
    candidate: &mut CandidatePageTables<'_, M>,
    allocator: &mut FrameAllocator,
    stack_start: u64,
    mapped_pages: usize,
) {
    for page in (0..mapped_pages).rev() {
        let virtual_address = stack_start + page as u64 * PAGE_SIZE;
        // SAFETY: Stack setup keeps IF clear and this candidate is the active
        // root; the frame is not returned until `invlpg` completes.
        let frame = unsafe { candidate.unmap_owned_page_active(virtual_address) }
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure());
        deallocate_or_halt(allocator, frame);
    }
}

fn reap_exited_stacks<M: CandidatePageTableMemory>(
    runtime: &mut KernelThreadRuntime,
    candidate: &mut CandidatePageTables<'_, M>,
    allocator: &mut FrameAllocator,
) {
    for slot in 0..MAX_THREADS {
        let Some(thread) = runtime.thread_ids[slot] else {
            continue;
        };
        if runtime.policy.state(thread) != Ok(ThreadState::Exited) {
            continue;
        }
        let stack_start =
            runtime.stack_virtual_starts[slot].unwrap_or_else(|| halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure());
        rollback_stack(candidate, allocator, stack_start, THREAD_STACK_PAGES);
        runtime
            .policy
            .reap(thread)
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure());
        runtime.thread_ids[slot] = None;
        runtime.stack_virtual_starts[slot] = None;
        runtime.entries[slot] = None;
        runtime.arguments[slot] = 0;
        runtime.deadlines[slot] = None;
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
fn cancel_unstarted_threads(runtime: &mut KernelThreadRuntime) {
    loop {
        match runtime.policy.dispatch() {
            Ok(Some(_)) => {
                if runtime.policy.exit_current().is_err() {
                    halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure();
                }
            }
            Ok(None) => return,
            Err(_) => halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure(),
        }
    }
}

fn deallocate_or_halt(allocator: &mut FrameAllocator, frame: Frame) {
    if let Err(failure) = allocator.deallocate(frame) {
        kprintln!("thread stack frame release failed: {:?}", failure.error);
        halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure();
    }
}

fn halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure() -> ! {
    loop {
        // SAFETY: Losing stack-frame ownership is fatal; stop without touching
        // any potentially inconsistent scheduler or allocator state.
        unsafe { asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

extern "C" fn kernel_thread_trampoline() -> ! {
    let runtime_pointer: *mut KernelThreadRuntime;
    let slot: usize;
    // SAFETY: The initial stack frame restores the runtime pointer in R13 and
    // the generation-checked policy slot index in R14 before this entry.
    unsafe {
        asm!("mov {}, r13", out(reg) runtime_pointer, options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags));
        asm!("mov {}, r14", out(reg) slot, options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags));
    }
    let (entry, argument) = {
        // SAFETY: The runtime is live on the retained bootstrap stack and the
        // selected slot was initialized before its context became dispatchable.
        let runtime = unsafe { &*runtime_pointer };
        let entry = runtime.entries[slot].unwrap_or_else(|| halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure());
        (entry, runtime.arguments[slot])
    };
    // New cooperative contexts start with IF clear. Enable the already-verified
    // timer route only after their descriptor and runtime state are available.
    // SAFETY: The scheduler installs no thread until the caller has configured
    // the timer and registered its bounded non-scheduling handler.
    unsafe { asm!("sti", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    entry(runtime_pointer.cast(), argument);
    // SAFETY: This thread's entry returned normally; mark it exited and switch
    // away before its stack can be reclaimed by the bootstrap context.
    unsafe { exit_current(runtime_pointer) }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
extern "C" fn waiter_thread(runtime: *mut (), _argument: usize) {
    THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(1, Ordering::Release);
    if !wait_for_event(runtime) || THREAD_TEST_TRACE.load(Ordering::Acquire) != 2 {
        THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(99, Ordering::Release);
        return;
    }
    THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(3, Ordering::Release);
    if !sleep_for_ticks(runtime, 2) || THREAD_TEST_TRACE.load(Ordering::Acquire) != 4 {
        THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(99, Ordering::Release);
        return;
    }
    THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(5, Ordering::Release);
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
extern "C" fn signaler_thread(runtime: *mut (), _argument: usize) {
    if THREAD_TEST_TRACE.load(Ordering::Acquire) != 1 {
        THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(99, Ordering::Release);
        return;
    }
    THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(2, Ordering::Release);
    if !wake_event(runtime) {
        THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(99, Ordering::Release);
        return;
    }
    yield_current(runtime);
    if THREAD_TEST_TRACE.load(Ordering::Acquire) != 3 {
        THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(99, Ordering::Release);
        return;
    }
    THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(4, Ordering::Release);
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
fn wait_for_event(runtime_pointer: *mut ()) -> bool {
    // SAFETY: This is an ordinary cooperative thread, never an IRQ handler.
    unsafe { block_current(runtime_pointer.cast(), None) }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
fn sleep_for_ticks(runtime_pointer: *mut (), delay: u64) -> bool {
    if delay == 0 {
        return true;
    }
    // SAFETY: The runtime pointer is restored from this thread's initial context;
    // the runtime remains alive until every thread has exited and been reaped.
    unsafe { block_current(runtime_pointer.cast(), Some(delay)) }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
fn wake_event(runtime_pointer: *mut ()) -> bool {
    let flags = disable_interrupts();
    // SAFETY: IF is clear and only the current cooperative thread mutates policy.
    let result = unsafe {
        let runtime = &mut *runtime_pointer.cast::<KernelThreadRuntime>();
        runtime.policy.wake_one(runtime.event_queue).is_ok()
    };
    restore_interrupts(flags);
    result
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-kernel-threads")]
fn yield_current(runtime_pointer: *mut ()) {
    let flags = disable_interrupts();
    let switch = unsafe {
        let runtime = &mut *runtime_pointer.cast::<KernelThreadRuntime>();
        let Some(current) = runtime.policy.current() else {
            restore_interrupts(flags);
            return;
        };
        let old_context = runtime.current_context;
        let next = match runtime.policy.yield_current() {
            Ok(next) => next,
            Err(_) => {
                THREAD_TEST_TRACE.store(99, Ordering::Release);
                restore_interrupts(flags);
                return;
            }
        };
        let next_context = next.slot_index() + 1;
        runtime.current_context = next_context;
        if current == next {
            None
        } else {
            Some((
                core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(runtime.saved_rsp[old_context]),
                runtime.saved_rsp[next_context],
            ))
        }
    };
    if let Some((old_rsp, new_rsp)) = switch {
        // SAFETY: The selected contexts are cooperative same-CPU kernel stacks;
        // temporary references to the scheduler ended before the switch.
        unsafe { rustix_arch_context_switch(old_rsp, new_rsp as *mut usize) };
    }
    restore_interrupts(flags);
}

unsafe fn block_current(runtime_pointer: *mut KernelThreadRuntime, delay: Option<u64>) -> bool {
    let flags = disable_interrupts();
    let switch = {
        // SAFETY: Called from one cooperative thread with IF clear; the state
        // references are scoped entirely before the context switch.
        let runtime = unsafe { &mut *runtime_pointer };
        let Some(current) = runtime.policy.current() else {
            restore_interrupts(flags);
            return false;
        };
        let slot = current.slot_index();
        let queue = if let Some(delay) = delay {
            let deadline = runtime.ticks.ticks().saturating_add(delay);
            runtime.deadlines[slot] = Some(deadline);
            runtime.timer_queues[slot]
        } else {
            runtime.event_queue
        };
        let next = match runtime.policy.sleep_current(queue) {
            Ok(next) => next,
            Err(_) => {
                runtime.deadlines[slot] = None;
                restore_interrupts(flags);
                return false;
            }
        };
        let next_context = next.map_or(0, |thread| thread.slot_index() + 1);
        let old_context = runtime.current_context;
        runtime.current_context = next_context;
        Some((
            core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(runtime.saved_rsp[old_context]),
            runtime.saved_rsp[next_context],
        ))
    };
    if let Some((old_rsp, new_rsp)) = switch {
        // SAFETY: The current thread is blocked and cannot be selected until a
        // later wake; the target is either a ready thread or the bootstrap stack.
        unsafe { rustix_arch_context_switch(old_rsp, new_rsp as *mut usize) };
    }
    restore_interrupts(flags);
    true
}

unsafe fn exit_current(runtime_pointer: *mut KernelThreadRuntime) -> ! {
    let flags = disable_interrupts();
    let (old_rsp, new_rsp) = {
        // SAFETY: This is the current thread's normal return path, with IF clear.
        let runtime = unsafe { &mut *runtime_pointer };
        let old_context = runtime.current_context;
        match runtime.policy.exit_current() {
            Ok(next) => {
                let next_context = next.map_or(0, |thread| thread.slot_index() + 1);
                runtime.current_context = next_context;
                (
                    core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(runtime.saved_rsp[old_context]),
                    runtime.saved_rsp[next_context],
                )
            }
            Err(_) => halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure(),
        }
    };
    // SAFETY: The exited context is never dispatched again; the target is a
    // different ready thread or the retained bootstrap stack.
    unsafe { rustix_arch_context_switch(old_rsp, new_rsp as *mut usize) };
    restore_interrupts(flags);
    halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure()
}

fn disable_interrupts() -> u64 {
    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: Bootstrap and cooperative threads execute at CPL 0; RFLAGS is
    // saved before CLI and the stack operation is balanced.
    unsafe { asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", "cli", out(reg) flags) };
    flags
}

fn restore_interrupts(flags: u64) {
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        // SAFETY: The caller only restores the prior IF state after its critical
        // section and after the selected stack/context is fully established.
        unsafe { asm!("sti", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

unsafe fn rustix_arch_context_switch(old_rsp: *mut usize, new_rsp: *mut usize) {
    // SAFETY: The runtime maintains valid saved stack frames and distinct live
    // contexts. Cooperative callers hold IF clear; the timer caller is already
    // in an interrupt gate with IF clear and suspends only its own IRQ call stack.
    unsafe { crate::arch::x86_64::context::context_switch(old_rsp, new_rsp) };
}

/// Advance scheduler deadlines/events and preempt the current thread if another
/// context is ready. Called only after the timer IRQ has sent APIC EOI.
pub(crate) fn timer_interrupt() {
    let runtime_pointer = ACTIVE_RUNTIME.load(Ordering::Acquire);
    if runtime_pointer.is_null() {
        return;
    }

    // The interrupt gate has cleared IF. Every ordinary scheduler mutation also
    // disables IF before borrowing this runtime, so the single CPU cannot observe
    // a partially updated scheduler state here.
    let switch = unsafe {
        let runtime = &mut *runtime_pointer;
        runtime.wake_ready_events();
        let Some(current) = runtime.policy.current() else {
            return;
        };
        let old_context = runtime.current_context;
        if old_context != current.slot_index() + 1 {
            halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure();
        }
        let next = runtime
            .policy
            .preempt_current()
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure());
        let next_context = next.slot_index() + 1;
        runtime.current_context = next_context;
        if next == current {
            None
        } else {
            Some((
                core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(runtime.saved_rsp[old_context]),
                runtime.saved_rsp[next_context],
            ))
        }
    };
    if let Some((old_rsp, new_rsp)) = switch {
        // SAFETY: The interrupted thread's full IRQ frame remains on its own
        // stack below this call. This saves the handler stack and resumes another
        // context; the interrupted thread later returns through its own IRETQ.
        unsafe { rustix_arch_context_switch(old_rsp, new_rsp as *mut usize) };
    }
}

struct LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader for LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'_> {
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn read_entry(&self, table_physical: u64, index: u16) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let table_end = table_physical
            .checked_add(rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        if !self.memory_map.range_is_within_region_kind(
            table_physical,
            table_end,
            rustix_kernel::memory::RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable,
        ) {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::NotLimineMapped);
        }
        let table_address = self.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            self.hhdm_offset,
            table_physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )?;
        let entry_address = table_address
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The complete table page was restricted to bootloader-reclaimable
        // memory and its HHDM address arithmetic was checked. The reader relies
        // on the Limine base-revision-3 mapping contract and never returns a ref.
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }
}

struct LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

// SAFETY: `prepare_table` accepts only an allocator-issued frame and validates
// its complete usable span and HHDM address. Handles are only used while the
// candidate retains the frame token and this unique backend borrow.
unsafe impl rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory for LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_> {
    type PreparedTable = u64;
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn prepare_table(
        &mut self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
    ) -> Result<Self::PreparedTable, Self::Error> {
        frame.hhdm_address(
            self.memory_map,
            self.hhdm_offset,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )
    }

    unsafe fn read_entry(
        &self,
        table: Self::PreparedTable,
        index: u16,
    ) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
